open_points.subject: artifact publication versus project lifecycle changes
open_points.text: Every publish and every withdrawal on one project's pointers is serialised with the others
open_points.question: What orders a publish or withdrawal against a concurrent archive, anonymisation or whole deletion of the same project, especially for an owner call not covered by A10's agent-call ordering?
options: Serialize pointer changes with every project lifecycle change
Permit whichever transaction commits first
Recheck project lifecycle immediately before the pointer transaction commits
open_points.default_guess: Serialize all pointer and project-lifecycle changes for the project, then evaluate the operation against the resulting state.

open_points.subject: owner-session cookie scope
open_points.text: carried by a cookie that scripts cannot read, sent only over HTTPS when the interface is reached from another machine, and only to Registry's own origin
open_points.question: What exact cookie domain, path, SameSite and Secure rules implement “only to Registry's own origin,” given that browser cookies are not scoped by port and local access may use HTTP?
options: Host-only, Registry-specific path, HttpOnly and SameSite=Strict; Secure only on HTTPS sessions
Host-only root-path cookie, HttpOnly and SameSite=Lax
Require HTTPS for every owner-interface session and always set Secure
open_points.default_guess: Use a host-only, Registry-specific-path, HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict cookie, with Secure whenever the session is served over HTTPS.

open_points.subject: multiple owner sign-ins
open_points.text: The owner signs in with the owner credential and receives an owner session
open_points.question: Does a successful sign-in leave earlier owner sessions valid, or invalidate some or all of them?
options: Allow multiple independent sessions until each expires or signs out
Invalidate every earlier owner session
Replace only an existing session carried by the signing-in browser
open_points.default_guess: Allow multiple independent owner sessions, since no rule says a new sign-in ends an existing one.

open_points.subject: rejected replacement import upload
open_points.text: at most one uploaded import file, replaced by the next upload
open_points.question: Does an upload refused for size, unreadable format or another upload-time failure replace and drop the session's previously retained file and invalidate confirmations bound to it?
options: Only a successfully accepted upload replaces the retained file
Every upload attempt replaces the retained file before validation
Every upload attempt drops the old file, but a refused new file is not retained
open_points.default_guess: Only an upload that passes the upload-time size and format checks replaces the retained file.

open_points.subject: import file digest
open_points.text: The mapping names the file by its digest
open_points.question: Which digest algorithm is used, and is it computed over the exact uploaded bytes or over a canonicalised parsed representation?
options: A specified cryptographic digest of the exact uploaded bytes
A specified digest of a canonical parsed representation
A backend-selected digest and representation
open_points.default_guess: Use SHA-256 over the exact uploaded bytes and represent it in one canonical encoding.

open_points.subject: uploaded files in concurrent owner sessions
open_points.text: at most one uploaded import file, replaced by the next upload and dropped when the import is accepted
open_points.question: When one owner session successfully imports, are uploaded files retained by other owner sessions dropped immediately, or do they remain until those sessions end?
options: Drop every session's uploaded import file when the migration closure is committed
Drop only the file used by the accepting session
Leave every file to its own session lifetime
open_points.default_guess: Drop every retained import file when the migration closure is committed, because no further import can be accepted.

open_points.subject: same-day retry after a failed backup run
open_points.text: if no backup was made that UTC day; there is at most one run per UTC day
open_points.question: If today's run fails and Registry restarts later that same UTC day, must it retry because no backup was made, or must it wait because a run already occurred?
options: At most one attempt per UTC day, so retry the next day
Retry on restart until one checked backup succeeds that day
Permit one scheduled attempt plus one restart retry
open_points.default_guess: Treat “run” as an attempt and wait until the next UTC day's run after a failure.

open_points.subject: backup encryption and tamper detection
open_points.text: Each backup is encrypted with the backup key
open_points.question: Must backup encryption authenticate the ciphertext and metadata, and what must happen when authentication fails or the wrong key is supplied?
options: Require authenticated encryption covering the backup and all metadata; refuse and delete a newly made backup on authentication failure
Require confidentiality only and rely on the store integrity check
Leave the encryption construction and tamper behaviour to the backend
open_points.default_guess: Require authenticated encryption covering both contents and metadata, and treat authentication failure as a failed backup or refused restore.

open_points.subject: audit sequence after restoring an older backup
open_points.text: numbering continues from the backup's last number
open_points.question: How can numbering continue from the backup while M09 and A15 require sequence numbers to be one more than the last ever written and never reused, including numbers written after the backup but lost during restore?
options: Allow reuse of sequence numbers belonging to changes lost by restore
Keep a durable high-water mark outside backups and restore it separately
Advance to a new sequence namespace or epoch after restore
open_points.default_guess: Preserve a durable high-water mark outside the restored store and continue above every sequence number ever issued.

open_points.subject: migration closure after restoring a pre-import backup
open_points.text: Every change after the backup's instant is lost
open_points.question: If the restored backup predates the successful one-time import, is the missing migration closure reconstructed so the operation remains closed, or may Registry accept another import?
options: Reconstruct the closure from an external recovery record before serving
Allow the import again because the closure and imported records were rolled back
Forbid service enablement until the owner explicitly marks the migration closed
open_points.default_guess: Require the owner to restore or re-establish the migration closure before enabling normal service.

open_points.subject: audit erasures after restore
open_points.text: brings each Customer and project to the state the owner's own record of the retention review gives for it now
open_points.question: How are audit entries erased after the backup's instant removed again after restore, since the reconciliation rule mentions only Customers and projects?
options: The owner reruns the applicable audit-date erasure before enabling tokens
The recovery procedure also carries an audit-retention cutoff and applies it automatically
Restored audit entries may remain until the next periodic review
open_points.default_guess: Require the owner to reapply the latest audit erasure cutoff during the owner-only recovery phase.

open_points.subject: verification of post-restore reconciliation
open_points.text: Registry, which no longer holds those changes, cannot list them or tell when this is done
open_points.question: What prevents service tokens from being enabled before every required post-backup erasure, restriction and relationship state has been reapplied?
options: Nothing in Registry; the owner is solely responsible
A separate signed recovery checklist or state gates token enablement
Registry imports a recovery manifest and verifies completion
open_points.default_guess: Treat this as an explicit external operational control, while acknowledging Registry cannot enforce the stated precondition.

open_points.subject: partial backup files after interruption
open_points.text: A backup or a deletion that fails leaves no partial file
open_points.question: How are process crashes or host failures during backup publication distinguished from valid backups and cleaned up on the next start or run?
options: Write under a temporary name and atomically publish only after verification; clean stale temporary files
Scan and validate every file at the next run
Depend on the backend to make backup writes atomic
open_points.default_guess: Write to a recognisable temporary file, verify it, atomically rename it, and remove stale temporary files at startup or the next run.

open_points.subject: security review after the A19 change
open_points.text: A change to a decision a category names reopens this review.
open_points.question: A19 is named by injection_interpreted_input and browser_boundary and has changed; has A21 been rerun against the revised rule, or is its “PERFORMED” result currently reopened?
options: A21 is reopened until the revised A19 is reviewed and accepted
The displayed A21 review already covers the revised A19
Only the injection_interpreted_input category is reopened
open_points.default_guess: Treat A21 as reopened and rerun at least every category that references A19 before marking the review performed again.
